hints.title: Lookahead Subgroup Sizing Obstacle
hints.text: Reversing blindly can alter an incomplete trailing segment. How can you verify that at least k nodes remain before inverting their references?

hints.title: Subgroup Boundary Invariant
hints.text: Check if k nodes remain from the current group start. If yes, reverse those k nodes, reconnect with the preceding tail and following head, then continue.

hints.title: In-Place Sub-segment Inversion Procedure
hints.text: Use a dummy head. In a loop, advance a probe pointer k times from groupPrev. If fewer than k nodes remain, break. Otherwise, reverse the k nodes between groupPrev and the next group start. Splice the reversed segment into the list and advance groupPrev to the new tail.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def reverseKGroup(self, head: Optional[ListNode], k: int) -> Optional[ListNode]:
        dummy = ListNode(0, head)
        group_prev = dummy
        while True:
            kth = group_prev
            for _ in range(k):
                kth = kth.next
                if not kth:
                    return dummy.next
            group_next = kth.next
            prev, curr = kth.next, group_prev.next
            while curr != group_next:
                nxt = curr.next
                curr.next = prev
                prev = curr
                curr = nxt
            tail = group_prev.next
            group_prev.next = kth
            group_prev = tail
```

variables: N: number of nodes in list (1 <= N <= 5000)
complexity.notes: Each node is inspected by the probe and rewired exactly once.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Buffering nodes in an auxiliary array violates strict O(1) in-place memory constraints.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Lookahead probe checks node sufficiency in O(1) space before starting the reversal loop.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Clean modular pointer reversal, correct retention of trailing nodes when count < k, and zero dangling pointers.
